input:
This executive summary provides an overview of delivery performance across the business and considers the scheduling investment that is currently under consideration. The firm is a contract packaging business that runs 4 plants and generates revenue of $72 million per year, so delivery reliability is a crucial part of the overall picture. Drawing on order records for 12 months, covering no fewer than 13085 orders in total, on-time delivery over the last two quarters was 90%, which falls short of the target of 95% that the business has set itself. It is worth noting that the shortfall is by no means evenly spread, highlighting the extent to which one site dominates the problem: Plant 2 accounts for 59% of late orders across the business as a whole.

The wider context is equally important. The order backlog currently stands at 3.5 weeks, compared with 1.7 weeks a year ago, and overtime cost was $1.9 million last year, up 17% on the year before, reflecting the growing pressure on the operation. A new scheduling system for all plants is quoted at $350k, while Plant 2 alone is $154k, and an internal estimate - not a vendor figure - puts the overtime reduction at Plant 2 at 15-20% in the first year. The recommendation under consideration is therefore to install at Plant 2 first and hold the other plants until Plant 2 results are reported, with the operations director owning the scheduling programme. This phased approach leverages the available evidence, focuses effort where the need is greatest, and ensures that any wider rollout at Plant 2's sister sites is grounded in reported results rather than projections, underscoring the value of a measured, evidence-led path forward.
